title: Letter to David Hale, 12–19 February 1841
handwriting: Handwriting of Lorenzo D. Wasson, Emma Smith, and JS
source_note: Lorenzo D. Wasson, Emma Smith, and JS, Letter, Nauvoo, Hancock Co., IL, to David Hale, Independence Township, Washington Co., PA, 12–19 Feb. 1841; handwriting of Lorenzo D. Wasson, Emma Smith, and JS; four pages. Transcription from digital color image, BYU. Two leaves, dimensions unknown. Pages appear approximately two-thirds as wide as they are tall and were possibly originally connected as a bifolium. The letter was written in ink, trifolded in letter style, and sent by post. The letter has several tears, including a large tear along the top right corner of the second page. It was repaired with adhesive tape along the fold lines. The original was in the possession of a descendant of the Hale family residing in San Diego, California, as late as the 1950s. Around that time, an acquaintance of that descendant made a typescript of the letter; the acquaintance later donated the typescript to the Church History Library in 1984.1 At some point, Brigham Young University obtained a scanned image of the original, likely at the same time it received other Hale family documents in 2010.2 The original is apparently in private possession.
